title: CAPF and Security Forces of India: Who Guards What: Quiz

questions.question: Which force guards the Indo-China border and is nicknamed 'Himveers'?
questions.rationale: ITBP was raised on 24 October 1962 and holds high-altitude posts along the India-China frontier. SSB looks after Nepal and Bhutan, which is the usual swap.

questions.question: The Sashastra Seema Bal guards which pair of borders?
questions.rationale: SSB covers about 1,751 km with Nepal and 699 km with Bhutan. Pakistan and Bangladesh belong to the BSF.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT under the Ministry of Home Affairs?
questions.rationale: The Coast Guard works under the Ministry of Defence (Coast Guard Act, 1978). The other three are MHA forces.

questions.question: The motto 'Seva aur Nishtha' (Service and Loyalty) belongs to:
questions.rationale: CRPF's motto is Service and Loyalty. BSF's is 'Duty unto Death' and CISF's is 'Protection and Security'.

questions.question: BSF was raised in which year, in the aftermath of the Indo-Pakistan conflict?
questions.rationale: BSF came into being on 1 December 1965. 1962 is ITBP and 1969 is CISF.

questions.question: Which force is the oldest paramilitary force of India, with the Army holding operational control?
questions.rationale: Assam Rifles traces back to the Cachar Levy of 1835. It is administered by the MHA but led operationally by the Army, and its DG is a Lieutenant General. CRPF dates only to 1939.

questions.question: Which force protects the Prime Minister and reports to the Cabinet Secretariat?
questions.rationale: The SPG (1985, SPG Act 1988) is a close-protection force under the Cabinet Secretariat. NSG, popularly 'Black Cats', is a counter-terror force under the MHA.

questions.question: Which statement about CRPF is correct?
options: It was founded in 1969 to protect industry
It began as the Crown Representative's Police in 1939
It is controlled by the Ministry of Defence
questions.rationale: CRPF started at Neemuch on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police and was renamed in 1949. Industrial protection is CISF's task.

questions.question: Valour Day, observed on 9 April, is associated with the fight at Sardar Post in 1965. Which force celebrates it?
questions.rationale: Valour Day commemorates the Sardar Post action in the Rann of Kutch by CRPF personnel. BSF's raising day is in December.

questions.question: In the order of raising years, which sequence (earliest to latest) is correct?
RAW, India's external intelligence agency, functions under the:
questions.rationale: RAW was formed in 1968 and sits in the Cabinet Secretariat. IB, the internal agency, is with the MHA.

questions.question: The National Investigation Agency was created after which event, by an Act of 2008?
questions.rationale: The NIA Act, 2008 followed the Mumbai attacks of November 2008. The agency investigates terror-related offences and falls under the MHA.

questions.question: The Railway Protection Force has which motto and parent ministry?
options: Seva aur Nishtha; Ministry of Railways
questions.rationale: RPF (Act of 1957) carries 'Yasho Labhasva' (Attain honour) and is under the Railways. 'Vayam Rakshamah' is the Coast Guard's motto.

questions.question: Which of these force and role pairs is correct?
questions.rationale: NDRF was constituted on 19 January 2006 under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. Airports and the Delhi Metro are CISF duties; China border is ITBP.

questions.question: CBI, whose motto is 'Industry, Impartiality, Integrity', is administratively under:
questions.rationale: CBI falls under DoPT and draws power from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. NIA, the terror-case agency, is with the MHA.
